title: Extremal Least Common Multiples in Rows of Pascal's Triangle
summary: For $r \ge 0$, let $\mathcal P_r=\{\binom{r}{0},\binom{r}{1},\ldots,\binom{r}{\lfloor r/2\rfloor}\}$ be the set of distinct entries in row $r$ of Pascal's triangle. We study the least possible least common multiple of $n$ entries chosen from one row, with the row itself also free: $a(n)=\min_{r\ge0,\ S\subseteq\mathcal P_r,\ |S|=n}\operatorname{lcm}(S)$. Whereas the least common multiple of an entire row is given by a classical identity of Farhi, allowing both the row and the selected coefficients to vary creates a different optimization problem.
